Define the mission

Your requirements shape the hardware plan.

Capacity estimate includes a 25% reserve. Enter measured average current for a useful estimate.

Hardware requirements

Wiring map

Dual H-bridge with two direction inputs and one PWM input per motor. Tie grounds together; use a separate motor supply.

Match driver logic voltage to the controller. Size the driver for each motor’s stall current. Connect driver enable/standby per its datasheet. Never power motors from GPIO.

Give your robot its first instructions.

Bench-test starter: motors remain stopped at startup. Lift the wheels before testing. Mission sensors need calibration and integration; autonomy is not generated.

Reference: Arduino PWM · Pico MicroPython · ESP32 MicroPython

From workbench to working robot

  1. Define your mission

    Choose your robot family and requirements in Robot purpose, then select a controller in Electronics. Confirm motor torque, stall current, driver ratings, and battery voltage against actual component datasheets.

  2. Make your parts

    Adjust a template and export STL. Import in millimeters into your slicer, check bed fit, and choose layer height, walls, and infill. The plate uses square mounting holes; print a fit sample first.

  3. Wire and verify

    Follow the generated pin map. Use appropriate supply regulation, a fuse, accessible power disconnect, and common ground. 3.3 V controllers require compatible sensor output levels.

  4. Bring up the firmware

    For Uno, open the .ino in Arduino IDE and select Uno. For ESP32/Pico, install the appropriate MicroPython firmware, then save main.py on the board. Use the command format documented in the generated code. Mobile platforms use F/B/L/R/S; arms and pan/tilt mounts use channel,pulse_us. Legged and gantry projects currently export configuration scaffolds.

  5. Test and iterate

    Check wheel direction with wheels raised. Movement stops after 500 ms without a new command. Integrate and calibrate mission sensors before floor testing. These templates are starting parts and firmware, not a validated robot assembly.
